regiones/cerdena-corcega/eras.2.resumen.texto: Rome takes both islands after the First Punic War; they supply grain and serve as a place of exile.

regiones/cerdena-corcega/eras.3.resumen.texto: The Vandals occupy the islands in the 5th century and Byzantium recovers them in 534; Arab raids isolate them from Constantinople.

regiones/cerdena-corcega/eras.4.resumen.texto: Sardinia is governed as four judicates (Cagliari, Arborea, Torres and Gallura); Pisa and Genoa contest the islands, and Aragon conquers Sardinia from 1323.

regiones/cerdena-corcega/eras.5.resumen.texto: Sardinia is a kingdom of the Crown of Aragon and later of Spain; Corsica remains under Genoa, with Pasquale Paoli's Corsican Republic from 1755.

regiones/cerdena-corcega/eras.6.resumen.texto: Genoa cedes Corsica to France in 1768; Sardinia, Savoyard from 1720, gives its name to the kingdom that unifies Italy in 1861.

fuentes/confesiones/resumen.texto: A spiritual autobiography in thirteen books, written as a long prayer to God: his childhood in Thagaste, his studies in Carthage, Manichaeism, Neoplatonism in Milan and his conversion in 386. The last books meditate on memory, time and creation.

fuentes/confesiones/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first great autobiography of Western literature and contains the most cited analysis of time in medieval philosophy.

fuentes/confesiones/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by E. B. Pusey (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/ciudad-de-dios/resumen.texto: A reply in twenty-two books to the pagans who blamed Christianity for the sack of Rome in 410. It contrasts the earthly city, founded on love of self, with the city of God, founded on love of God, which coexist intermingled until the end of history.

fuentes/ciudad-de-dios/por_que_importa.texto: It was the foundation of the theology of history and of political thought throughout the Latin Middle Ages.

fuentes/ciudad-de-dios/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by Marcus Dods, vol. I (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/ciudad-de-dios/leer.2.titulo.texto: English translation by Marcus Dods, vol. II (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/consolacion-de-la-filosofia/resu.texto: A dialogue in prose and verse written in prison while Boethius awaited his execution. Philosophy, personified as a woman, shows him that fortune is unstable, that true happiness is God and that divine foreknowledge does not cancel human freedom.

fuentes/consolacion-de-la-filosofia/por_.texto: After the Bible, it was one of the most copied and translated books of the Middle Ages: Alfred the Great, Chaucer and Jean de Meun rendered it into their languages.

fuentes/consolacion-de-la-filosofia/leer.texto: Latin text with English translation (Rand and Stewart, 1918; Project Gutenberg)
English translation by H. R. James (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/comentarios-a-la-isagoge/resumen.texto: Two commentaries by Boethius on Porphyry's introduction to Aristotle's Categories. In the second he raises the question of whether genera and species exist in reality or only in the understanding.

fuentes/comentarios-a-la-isagoge/por_que.texto: That passage gave rise to the problem of universals, the great debate of medieval philosophy between realists and nominalists.

fuentes/instituciones-de-casiodoro/resum.texto: Study guide for the monks of Vivarium in two books: the first on reading the Bible and its commentators; the second, a summary of the seven liberal arts.

fuentes/instituciones-de-casiodoro/por_q.texto: It made the copying and study of texts a monastic task and passed on to the Middle Ages the program of the trivium and the quadrivium.

fuentes/regla-de-san-benito/resumen.texto: Regulations for life in the monastery in seventy-three chapters: obedience to the abbot, hours of prayer, manual labor, reading, food, sleep and the admission of novices, in a spirit of moderation.

fuentes/regla-de-san-benito/por_que_impo.texto: It was the rule of nearly all the monasteries of the West from the 9th century; it ordered the life of the institutions that preserved written culture.

fuentes/corpus-dionysiacum/resumen.texto: Four treatises and ten letters attributed to Dionysius, the Athenian converted by Saint Paul, though written c. 500 by a Christian Neoplatonist author: The Divine Names, The Mystical Theology, The Celestial Hierarchy and The Ecclesiastical Hierarchy.

fuentes/corpus-dionysiacum/por_que_impor.texto: With the prestige of a disciple of the apostles, it brought negative theology and the idea of hierarchy into Christianity; it was translated by Eriugena and Grosseteste and commented on by Thomas Aquinas.

fuentes/moralia-in-job/resumen.texto: Commentary in thirty-five books on the Book of Job, begun in Constantinople and finished in Rome, which reads each passage in a literal, allegorical and moral sense.

fuentes/moralia-in-job/por_que_importa.texto: It was the great handbook of Christian morality of the Early Middle Ages.

fuentes/dialogos-de-gregorio/resumen.texto: Four books of miracles and lives of Italian saints in dialogue form; the second is the only ancient biography of Benedict of Nursia.

fuentes/dialogos-de-gregorio/por_que_imp.texto: It is the main source on Saint Benedict and one of the books that shaped medieval devotion to miracles and purgatory.

fuentes/etimologias/resumen.texto: Encyclopedia in twenty books that explains each thing from the origin of its name: grammar, rhetoric, mathematics, medicine, law, chronology, theology, animals, the world, buildings, stones, war, ships and clothing. His disciple Braulio divided it into books after Isidore's death. Of the Gauls he repeats that their name comes from the whiteness of their skin, from Greek gala, “milk”, and he calls the Galatians Gauls (IX.2; XIV.4).

fuentes/etimologias/por_que_importa.texto: It was the reference book of the entire Middle Ages, with more than a thousand surviving manuscripts, and it transmitted much of ancient knowledge.

fuentes/historia-de-los-godos/titulo.texto: History of the Kings of the Goths, Vandals and Suevi

fuentes/historia-de-los-godos/resumen.texto: Brief history of the Germanic peoples of Hispania that opens with a “Praise of Spain”.

fuentes/historia-de-los-godos/por_que_im.texto: It is a main source for the Visigothic kingdom and for the birth of the idea of Hispania as the homeland of the Goths.

fuentes/fuente-del-conocimiento/resumen.texto: Work in three parts: the philosophical chapters, a vocabulary of Aristotelian logic; a catalog of heresies, with one of the first Christian texts on Islam; and the Exposition of the Orthodox Faith, a summary of Greek theology.

fuentes/fuente-del-conocimiento/por_que_.texto: Translated into Latin in the 12th century as De fide orthodoxa, it was one of the sources of Peter Lombard and Thomas Aquinas.

fuentes/historia-eclesiastica-de-beda/ti.texto: Ecclesiastical History of the English People

fuentes/historia-eclesiastica-de-beda/re.texto: History of the Christianization of the Anglo-Saxons from the arrival of Augustine of Canterbury in 597, with background from Roman Britain. It cites documents and witnesses and dates events from the Incarnation of Christ.

fuentes/historia-eclesiastica-de-beda/po.texto: It is the main source for English history before the 8th century and popularized the Christian era for dating. It is also the main source on the Picts, Britons and Irish of his time, told from the English side: the Scythian origin of the Picts and their succession through the female line (I.1), the massacre of the monks of Bangor at Chester (II.2) and the dispute over Easter (III.25), and it reproaches the Britons for not having preached to the Angles (I.22).

fuentes/computo-del-tiempo/resumen.texto: Treatise on chronology and practical astronomy: calendars, tides, the length of the day according to latitude and the calculation of the date of Easter, with a chronicle of the world.

fuentes/computo-del-tiempo/por_que_impor.texto: It established the method for calculating Easter and explained the tides by the Moon with its own observations; it was a textbook in the Carolingian schools.

fuentes/de-rerum-naturis/resumen.texto: Encyclopedia in twenty-two books based on Isidore's Etymologies, which adds to each thing its allegorical and moral meaning.

fuentes/de-rerum-naturis/por_que_importa.texto: It shows how ancient knowledge became a repertoire for reading the Bible; illustrated manuscripts from the 11th century survive.

fuentes/periphyseon/resumen.texto: Dialogue in five books between a master and his disciple that divides nature into four: that which creates and is not created (God), that which is created and creates (the ideas), that which is created and does not create (things) and that which neither creates nor is created (God as end). Everything proceeds from God and returns to him.

fuentes/periphyseon/por_que_importa.texto: It is the most ambitious philosophical system between Augustine and scholasticism. It was condemned in 1225 for its apparent pantheism.

fuentes/monologion/resumen.texto: Meditation written at the request of the monks of Bec that proves the existence and attributes of God “by reason alone”, without relying on the authority of Scripture, starting from the degrees of goodness in things.

fuentes/monologion/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the first medieval attempts at a purely rational theology, a model for scholasticism.

fuentes/proslogion/resumen.texto: Short meditation that seeks a single argument to prove that God exists: God is “that than which nothing greater can be thought”, and this cannot exist only in the understanding. It includes the objection of the monk Gaunilo and Anselm's reply.

fuentes/proslogion/por_que_importa.texto: It contains the so-called ontological argument, discussed by Thomas Aquinas, Descartes, Leibniz, Kant and 20th-century modal logic.

fuentes/cur-deus-homo/resumen.texto: Dialogue with the monk Boso that explains through necessary reasons why the Incarnation and death of Christ were necessary to repair the offense of sin.

fuentes/cur-deus-homo/por_que_importa.texto: Its satisfaction theory dominated Western theology of redemption.

fuentes/sic-et-non/resumen.texto: Collection of 158 theological questions with quotations from the Bible and the Church Fathers that seem to contradict each other, preceded by a prologue with rules for resolving the contradictions: distinguishing the senses of words, periods and the authenticity of texts.

fuentes/sic-et-non/por_que_importa.texto: Its method of setting authorities against each other and resolving them by reason is the basis of the scholastic “question”.

fuentes/historia-calamitatum/resumen.texto: Autobiographical letter to a friend in which Abelard recounts his successes as a teacher, his love for Heloise, his castration, the condemnation at Soissons and his troubles as abbot of Saint-Gildas, in Brittany. It opened his correspondence with Heloise.

fuentes/historia-calamitatum/por_que_imp.texto: It is one of the few medieval autobiographies and a direct source on the schools of Paris.

fuentes/historia-calamitatum/leer.1.titu.texto: English translation by Henry Adams Bellows (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/cartas-de-abelardo-y-eloisa/resu.texto: Correspondence between Heloise, abbess of the Paraclete, and Abelard. Heloise recalls their love, discusses marriage and asks for a rule for the nuns; Abelard replies with advice and a history of nuns.

fuentes/cartas-de-abelardo-y-eloisa/por_.texto: It is an exceptional testimony of the voice of an educated 12th-century woman; its authenticity was debated and is now generally accepted.

fuentes/etica-de-abelardo/resumen.texto: Treatise on ethics that places the moral value of acts in intention and consent, not in the outward act or in desire.

fuentes/etica-de-abelardo/por_que_import.texto: It is the first systematic ethics of the Latin Middle Ages and one element in Bernard of Clairvaux's accusations against Abelard.

fuentes/didascalicon/resumen.texto: Study guide that orders all the sciences into theoretical, practical, mechanical and logical, and teaches how to read: the order of books, method and the student's discipline.

fuentes/didascalicon/por_que_importa.texto: It included the mechanical arts, such as weaving, navigation and agriculture, among the branches of knowledge, and was a model for classifications of the sciences.

fuentes/libros-de-las-sentencias/resumen.texto: Ordered compilation of texts from the Bible and the Fathers in four books: God and the Trinity; creation; the Incarnation and the virtues; the sacraments and the last things. Each doubtful passage is briefly resolved.

fuentes/libros-de-las-sentencias/por_que.texto: From the time Alexander of Hales used it in his lectures c. 1223, every master of theology had to comment on it; there are thousands of commentaries, including those of Thomas, Bonaventure, Scotus and Ockham.

fuentes/policraticus/resumen.texto: Treatise in eight books on the frivolities of courtiers and the duties of the prince. It compares the state to a body whose soul is the clergy and whose head is the prince, and justifies killing the tyrant.

fuentes/policraticus/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first great treatise of political theory of the Latin Middle Ages, with abundant quotations from classical authors.

fuentes/metalogicon/resumen.texto: Defense of the trivium, and above all of logic, against those who wanted to shorten studies. It describes the masters John heard in Paris and Chartres between 1136 and 1148.

fuentes/metalogicon/por_que_importa.texto: It is the main source on the 12th-century schools and one of the first presentations of the whole of Aristotle's logic in the West.

fuentes/cosmographia/resumen.texto: Account of creation in prose and verse: Nature asks Providence to order chaotic matter, and then, with the help of Urania and Physis, forms the human being.

fuentes/cosmographia/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great literary work of the Platonism of Chartres and Tours; it was read before Pope Eugene III.

fuentes/filosofia-del-mundo/resumen.texto: Treatise on natural philosophy that explains the cosmos, the elements, meteorology, geography and the human body through natural causes, based on the Timaeus and on medicine.

fuentes/filosofia-del-mundo/por_que_impo.texto: It is the clearest example of 12th-century naturalism: William called for seeking the reasons of things rather than settling for saying that God can do everything.

fuentes/heptateuchon/resumen.texto: Anthology of teaching texts for the seven liberal arts compiled by Thierry: grammar by Donatus and Priscian, rhetoric by Cicero, logic by Aristotle and Boethius, and arithmetic, geometry, music and astronomy.

fuentes/heptateuchon/por_que_importa.texto: It shows what was read in a 12th-century school; the Chartres manuscript was destroyed in the 1944 bombing, though photographs survive.

fuentes/anticlaudianus/resumen.texto: Allegorical poem in nine books: Nature wants to create the perfect man, and Prudence travels through the heavens, guided by the liberal arts and then by Theology, to ask God for a soul.

fuentes/anticlaudianus/por_que_importa.texto: It is a verse encyclopedia of 12th-century knowledge and a model for the allegory used by Dante.

fuentes/scivias/resumen.texto: Account and explanation of twenty-six visions on creation, redemption and the end of time. Hildegard dictated it to her secretary Volmar, and Pope Eugene III approved its reading at the Synod of Trier of 1147-1148.

fuentes/scivias/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the great works of medieval visionary literature; the Rupertsberg manuscript, illuminated under her direction, was lost in 1945 and a copy survives.

fuentes/physica/resumen.texto: Treatise on natural history and medicine on the healing properties of plants, elements, trees, stones, fish, birds, animals and metals, with names in German.

fuentes/physica/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the first works of natural history written in Germany and preserves popular knowledge of monastic medicine.

fuentes/concordia-de-joaquin/titulo.texto: Book of the Concordance of the New and Old Testaments

fuentes/concordia-de-joaquin/resumen.texto: Interpretation of history as a parallel between the two Testaments, which divides time into three states: of the Father, of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, the last about to begin.

fuentes/concordia-de-joaquin/por_que_imp.texto: Its prophecies fed the Spiritual Franciscans and European millenarianism for centuries.

fuentes/sobre-el-amor-de-dios/resumen.texto: Treatise on why and how God should be loved, with the four degrees of love, from the love of oneself for one's own sake to loving oneself only for God's sake.

fuentes/sobre-el-amor-de-dios/por_que_im.texto: It is a fundamental work of Cistercian mysticism.

fuentes/fuente-de-la-vida/idioma_origina.texto: Arabic (original lost); survives in Latin and in a Hebrew summary

fuentes/fuente-de-la-vida/resumen.texto: Neoplatonic dialogue between master and disciple according to which everything created, except God, is composed of matter and form, even angels and souls; the divine will is the mediator of creation.

fuentes/fuente-de-la-vida/por_que_import.texto: Translated into Latin in Toledo by Gundissalinus and John of Spain, it influenced the Franciscans; not until 1846 was it known that its author was the Jewish poet Ibn Gabirol.

fuentes/collar-de-la-paloma/resumen.texto: Treatise on love and lovers in thirty chapters, with anecdotes from the Córdoba of his youth and his own poems: the signs of love, love at first sight, fidelity, separation and death.

fuentes/collar-de-la-paloma/por_que_impo.texto: It is an exceptional portrait of Andalusi society at the end of the caliphate.

fuentes/deberes-de-los-corazones/idioma_.texto: Arabic (translated into Hebrew in the 12th century)

fuentes/deberes-de-los-corazones/resumen.texto: Treatise on religious ethics in ten “gates” ranging from the unity of God to trust, humility, repentance and the love of God, in order to fulfill the inner duties, not only the outward ones.

fuentes/deberes-de-los-corazones/por_que.texto: It is one of the most widely read ethical works of Judaism and shows the influence of Neoplatonism and Sufism.

fuentes/cuzari/resumen.texto: Dialogue in five parts based on the conversion of the king of the Khazars to Judaism: the king listens to a philosopher, a Christian, a Muslim and a rabbi, and chooses the faith of the last, founded on history and revelation.

fuentes/cuzari/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great defense of Judaism against Aristotelian philosophy, Christianity and Islam.

fuentes/fe-sublime/resumen.texto: Treatise that explains the Jewish faith through Aristotle's physics, psychology and metaphysics, by way of Avicenna.

fuentes/fe-sublime/por_que_importa.texto: It opened the Jewish Aristotelianism that Maimonides would bring to its culmination.

fuentes/libro-de-la-tradicion/resumen.texto: Chronicle of the chain of Jewish sages from Moses to his own time, with the history of the academies of Mesopotamia and of the sages of al-Andalus, including the legend of the four captives.

fuentes/libro-de-la-tradicion/por_que_im.texto: It is the main source for the history of the Jews of Sepharad from the 10th to the 12th centuries.

fuentes/regimen-del-solitario/resumen.texto: Unfinished treatise on how the philosopher can attain happiness, union with the active intellect, even while living in an imperfect city: as an isolated “plant”.

fuentes/regimen-del-solitario/por_que_im.texto: It is the first great work of Andalusi political philosophy; Averroes and Moses of Narbonne commented on it.

fuentes/filosofo-autodidacta/resumen.texto: Philosophical novel about a boy raised by a gazelle on a desert island who, through observation and reason alone, arrives at physics, astronomy and the knowledge of God. When he meets other people, he discovers that their religion expresses the same truth through symbols.

fuentes/filosofo-autodidacta/por_que_imp.texto: Translated into Latin as Philosophus autodidactus in 1671, it influenced the European Enlightenment thinkers and is considered one of the sources of Robinson Crusoe.

fuentes/filosofo-autodidacta/leer.0.titu.texto: English translation by Simon Ockley, 1708 (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/incoherencia-de-la-incoherencia/.texto: Paragraph-by-paragraph reply to al-Ghazali's The Incoherence of the Philosophers, which had accused Avicenna and the Aristotelians of impiety. Averroes defends the eternity of the world and natural causality.
It is the great medieval defense of philosophy against theology.

fuentes/discurso-decisivo/resumen.texto: Legal opinion on whether Islamic law permits or commands the study of philosophy. Averroes answers that it makes it obligatory for those who are capable, because truth does not contradict truth, and distinguishes three kinds of people according to their way of reasoning.

fuentes/discurso-decisivo/por_que_import.texto: It is the classic text on the relationship between reason and revelation in Islam.

fuentes/gran-comentario-del-alma/idioma_.texto: Arabic (original largely lost); preserved in the Latin translation by Michael Scot

fuentes/gran-comentario-del-alma/resumen.texto: Line-by-line commentary on Aristotle's treatise On the Soul, in which Averroes holds that the material intellect, which receives universal forms, is one and the same for all human beings.

fuentes/gran-comentario-del-alma/por_que.texto: Its thesis of the unity of the intellect sparked Latin Averroism and the response of Thomas Aquinas.

fuentes/guia-de-perplejos/idioma_origina.texto: Judeo-Arabic (translated into Hebrew by Samuel ibn Tibbon in 1204)

fuentes/guia-de-perplejos/resumen.texto: Work in three parts for the believer trained in philosophy who feels perplexed by the anthropomorphisms of the Bible: it explains the names of God, negative theology, creation, prophecy, providence and the reasons for the commandments.

fuentes/guia-de-perplejos/por_que_import.texto: It is the masterpiece of medieval Jewish philosophy; translated into Latin, it was used by Albert the Great and Thomas Aquinas.

fuentes/guia-de-perplejos/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation by M. Friedländer (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/mishne-tora/resumen.texto: Code of all Jewish law in fourteen books, arranged by subject and written in clear Hebrew. Its first book summarizes the foundations of faith and philosophy.

fuentes/mishne-tora/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first complete code of Jewish law and remains a reference.

fuentes/zohar/soporte.texto: Manuscripts; printed in Mantua and Cremona in 1558-1560

fuentes/zohar/resumen.texto: Mystical commentary on the Torah presented as the teachings of Rabbi Simeon bar Yochai in 2nd-century Palestine. It sets out the doctrine of the sefirot, the emanations through which God manifests himself.

fuentes/zohar/por_que_importa.texto: It is the central work of Kabbalah; since the studies of Gershom Scholem, its main composition has been attributed to Moses de León in Castile.

fuentes/guerras-del-senor/resumen.texto: Treatise in six books on the immortality of the soul, dreams and prophecy, divine knowledge, providence, the heavenly bodies and creation. The fifth book is a treatise on astronomy with his own observations.

fuentes/guerras-del-senor/por_que_import.texto: It is the boldest work of Jewish Aristotelianism: Gersonides follows reason even against traditional interpretation.

fuentes/luz-del-senor/resumen.texto: Critique of the physics and metaphysics of Aristotle and Maimonides: it admits the void, the actual infinite and the possibility of many worlds, and places love, not the intellect, at the center of the relationship with God.

fuentes/luz-del-senor/por_que_importa.texto: It was one of the most profound critiques of Aristotle before modern science; Pico della Mirandola and Spinoza read it.

fuentes/libro-de-los-principios/resumen.texto: Exposition of the Jewish faith in three fundamental principles, the existence of God, revelation and retribution, from which the others are derived.

fuentes/libro-de-los-principios/por_que_.texto: It was widely read as a response to the pressure of the disputations and conversions of the early 15th century.

fuentes/disputa-de-barcelona-relato/titu.texto: Account of the Disputation of Barcelona

fuentes/disputa-de-barcelona-relato/resu.texto: Account that Nahmanides wrote, at the request of the bishop of Girona, of his debate before James I with the convert Pablo Christiani on whether the Messiah had come. The text earned him a trial and exile.

fuentes/disputa-de-barcelona-relato/por_.texto: It is the Jewish testimony of the most famous disputation of the Middle Ages; a brief Latin record also exists.

fuentes/division-de-la-filosofia/resumen.texto: Classification of the sciences that adds to the Latin liberal arts the sciences of the Arabic tradition, taken mainly from al-Farabi: physics, medicine, optics, engineering, politics and metaphysics.

fuentes/division-de-la-filosofia/por_que.texto: It introduced into Latin Europe the Arabic map of Aristotelian knowledge, which would later structure the faculties of arts.

fuentes/almagesto-latino/resumen.texto: Latin translation of Ptolemy's great treatise on astronomy, made from the Arabic version. It was what prompted Gerard's journey to Toledo, according to the notice written by his disciples.

fuentes/almagesto-latino/por_que_importa.texto: It was the most widely read version of the Almagest in Europe until the Renaissance.

fuentes/cuestiones-naturales/resumen.texto: Dialogue with his nephew on seventy-six questions about plants, animals, the human being, the Earth and the stars, which Adelard answers with “what was learned from the Arab masters” and with reason.

fuentes/cuestiones-naturales/por_que_imp.texto: It is a 12th-century manifesto in favor of investigating natural causes as opposed to authority.

fuentes/sobre-la-luz/resumen.texto: Short treatise according to which God created a point of light that, expanding in all directions, drew matter along with it and formed the spheres of the universe.

fuentes/sobre-la-luz/por_que_importa.texto: It is a cosmology of light that has been compared with modern theories of the origin of the universe; it shows Grosseteste's mathematical program.

fuentes/opus-maius/resumen.texto: Work in seven parts sent to Pope Clement IV: the causes of error, the relationship between philosophy and theology, the study of languages, mathematics and geography, optics, experimental science and moral philosophy.

fuentes/opus-maius/por_que_importa.texto: It is a program for the reform of learning that defends experience and mathematics, with one of the first European descriptions of gunpowder.

fuentes/suma-de-teologia/resumen.texto: Complete exposition of theology for beginners in three parts: God and creation; the human being, human acts, virtues and laws; and Christ and the sacraments. It is organized into some 3,000 articles with objections, a contrary argument, a response and replies to the objections. It was left unfinished.

fuentes/suma-de-teologia/por_que_importa.texto: It is the crowning work of scholasticism, with the five ways to God and the theory of natural law; from 1879 the Catholic Church put it forward as the basis of teaching.

fuentes/suma-de-teologia/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by the English Dominicans, First Part (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/suma-de-teologia/leer.2.titulo.texto: English translation, First Part of the Second Part (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/suma-de-teologia/leer.3.titulo.texto: English translation, Second Part of the Second Part (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/suma-contra-los-gentiles/soporte.texto: Parchment manuscripts; part of the autograph survives

fuentes/suma-contra-los-gentiles/resumen.texto: Defense of the faith in four books that starts from what reason can demonstrate about God, creation and the end of the human being, and goes on to what is known only through revelation.

fuentes/suma-contra-los-gentiles/por_que.texto: According to a late tradition, it was written for the Dominican missionaries who debated with Muslims and Jews in the Iberian Peninsula.

fuentes/el-ente-y-la-esencia/resumen.texto: Short early treatise for his fellow Dominicans that defines being, essence and the difference between essence and existence in creatures, separate substances and God.

fuentes/el-ente-y-la-esencia/por_que_imp.texto: It contains the central thesis of Thomist metaphysics: only in God is essence his own being.

fuentes/sobre-la-unidad-del-intelecto/ti.texto: On the Unity of the Intellect against the Averroists

fuentes/sobre-la-unidad-del-intelecto/re.texto: Polemical treatise against Averroes's thesis, upheld in Paris by Siger of Brabant, that there is a single intellect for all men. Thomas argues from texts of Aristotle that the intellect is a faculty of each soul.

fuentes/sobre-la-unidad-del-intelecto/po.texto: It is the central document of the Averroist crisis in Paris, from the same year as the condemnation of 1270.

fuentes/itinerario-de-la-mente/titulo.texto: The Journey of the Mind to God

fuentes/itinerario-de-la-mente/resumen.texto: Meditation written on Mount Alverna, where Francis received the stigmata, that describes six stages of ascent to God: through the vestiges in sensible things, through the image in the soul and through the light of God himself, up to ecstasy.

fuentes/itinerario-de-la-mente/por_que_i.texto: It is the best-known work of Franciscan theology, of Augustinian and Dionysian inspiration.

fuentes/sobre-la-eternidad-del-mundo-dac.texto: On the Eternity of the World
Treatise holding that the world had a beginning, according to faith, but that no philosopher can demonstrate this with natural arguments, because each science reasons from its own principles.
It is a classic defense of the autonomy of philosophy and one of the targets of the condemnation of 1277.

fuentes/condena-de-1277/soporte.texto: Episcopal decree preserved in manuscripts and in the Chartularium of the University of Paris

fuentes/condena-de-1277/resumen.texto: Decree of the bishop of Paris, dated 7 March 1277, that excommunicates anyone who teaches 219 theses: the eternity of the world, the unity of the intellect, that God cannot create other worlds or move the universe in a straight line, that happiness lies in this life, and others.

fuentes/condena-de-1277/por_que_importa.texto: It set the limits of philosophy in the universities and, according to a much-debated thesis of Pierre Duhem, paved the way for modern physics by forcing thinkers to consider possibilities that Aristotle denied.

fuentes/libro-del-gentil/titulo.texto: The Book of the Gentile and the Three Wise Men

fuentes/libro-del-gentil/idioma_original.texto: Catalan (versions in Latin, Castilian and Hebrew)

fuentes/libro-del-gentil/resumen.texto: Dialogue in a forest in which a Jewish, a Christian and a Muslim sage set out their faith to a gentile seeking comfort in the face of death, with arguments following the Lullian Art. At the end it is not said which religion he chooses.

fuentes/libro-del-gentil/por_que_importa.texto: It is an exceptional model of courteous dialogue among the three religions in the Middle Ages.

fuentes/arte-breve/resumen.texto: Abridged version of Llull's General Art: a system of nine principles, such as goodness, greatness or eternity, represented by letters and combined by means of figures and rotating wheels to answer any question.

fuentes/arte-breve/por_que_importa.texto: It inspired Nicholas of Cusa, Giordano Bruno and Leibniz, who saw in it a forerunner of his logical calculus.

fuentes/ordinatio/resumen.texto: Commentary on Peter Lombard's Sentences revised by Scotus for publication: the univocity of being, the proof of the existence of an infinite being, individuation and the will.

fuentes/ordinatio/por_que_importa.texto: It is the main work of Scotism, one of the great schools of scholasticism until the 18th century.

fuentes/suma-de-logica/resumen.texto: Complete manual of logic in three parts: terms and their signification, propositions and arguments. It explains how general terms signify individuals without there being common natures.

fuentes/suma-de-logica/por_que_importa.texto: It is the main treatise of nominalism and one of the greatest achievements of medieval logic.

fuentes/defensor-de-la-paz/resumen.texto: Treatise in three parts that, drawing on Aristotle's Politics, grounds law in the “human legislator”, the community of citizens, and holds that the Church has no coercive power and that the pope has no primacy by divine right.

fuentes/defensor-de-la-paz/por_que_impor.texto: It is one of the most radical political texts of the Middle Ages; John XXII condemned it in 1327 and it was read by the reformers of the 16th century.

fuentes/sermones-alemanes/resumen.texto: More than a hundred sermons in German on detachment, poverty of spirit, the ground of the soul and the birth of God in the soul.

fuentes/sermones-alemanes/por_que_import.texto: They are among the summits of mysticism and of German prose; several of their sentences were condemned in 1329.

fuentes/espejo-de-las-almas-simples/sopo.texto: Manuscripts in French, Latin, Italian and English

fuentes/espejo-de-las-almas-simples/resu.texto: Allegorical dialogue between the Soul, Love and Reason on seven states of the soul that lead it to be annihilated in God, beyond the virtues and the visible Church.

fuentes/espejo-de-las-almas-simples/por_.texto: Because of it, its author was burned at the stake in 1310; it circulated anonymously and Marguerite was not identified as its author until 1946.

fuentes/cuestiones-sobre-la-fisica/resum.texto: Commentary in the form of questions on Aristotle's Physics in which Buridan explains that the mover imparts to the projectile an impetus proportional to its speed and its quantity of matter, which decreases only through air resistance and gravity.

fuentes/cuestiones-sobre-la-fisica/por_q.texto: The theory of impetus was a step toward the concept of inertia; it was discussed by Oresme, Albert of Saxony and the young Galileo.

fuentes/libro-del-cielo-y-del-mundo/titu.texto: Book of the Heavens and the World

fuentes/libro-del-cielo-y-del-mundo/resu.texto: Annotated French translation of Aristotle's treatise On the Heavens, made for King Charles V. Oresme shows that neither experience nor reason proves that the Earth is at rest and that the heavens revolve.

fuentes/libro-del-cielo-y-del-mundo/por_.texto: It is one of the first scientific works in French and anticipates arguments of Copernicus and Galileo.

fuentes/tratado-de-la-moneda/idioma_orig.texto: Latin (with a French version by the author)

fuentes/tratado-de-la-moneda/resumen.texto: Treatise on the origin, nature and alterations of money, written when the kings of France were debasing it to finance the war: money belongs to the community, not to the prince, and altering it is a form of tyranny.

fuentes/tratado-de-la-moneda/por_que_imp.texto: It is one of the first treatises on monetary economics in Europe.

fuentes/tratado-de-las-proporciones/resu.texto: Treatise on dynamics proposing that speed increases arithmetically when the ratio of force to resistance increases geometrically, in order to correct the inconsistencies of Aristotle's law.

fuentes/tratado-de-las-proporciones/por_.texto: It opened the school of the Merton College Calculators, who studied motion mathematically.

fuentes/sobre-el-dominio-civil/resumen.texto: Treatise holding that all legitimate dominion comes from God and depends on grace, so that clergy in sin lose the right to their property and the civil power may take it from them.

fuentes/sobre-el-dominio-civil/por_que_i.texto: Gregory XI condemned eighteen theses taken from this work in 1377; its ideas passed to Bohemia with Hus.

fuentes/biblia-de-wyclif/resumen.texto: First complete translation of the Bible into English, made from the Latin Vulgate by Wycliffe's circle, in a very literal version and a revised one.

fuentes/biblia-de-wyclif/por_que_importa.texto: It was banned in 1409 and even so is one of the medieval English texts with the most surviving copies.

fuentes/sobre-la-iglesia-de-hus/resumen.texto: Treatise that defines the Church as the community of the predestined, not as the hierarchy, and denies that the pope is its necessary head if he lives in sin.

fuentes/sobre-la-iglesia-de-hus/por_que_.texto: It was the basis for Hus's condemnation at Constance in 1415.

fuentes/imitacion-de-cristo/resumen.texto: Devotional book in four parts that invites the reader to leave the vanities of the world, seek the inner life, find consolation in God and prepare the soul for communion.

fuentes/imitacion-de-cristo/por_que_impo.texto: It is the most representative work of the devotio moderna and one of the most translated books in history.

fuentes/imitacion-de-cristo/leer.1.titul.texto: English translation by William Benham (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/docta-ignorancia/resumen.texto: Treatise in three books that starts from knowing that we do not know: God, the absolute maximum, is beyond all proportion and in him opposites coincide; the universe is a limited maximum with no fixed center or circumference; Christ unites the two.

fuentes/docta-ignorancia/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the works that open modern philosophy; Cusa conceived it while returning from Constantinople in 1437.

fuentes/la-paz-de-la-fe/resumen.texto: Dialogue written after the news of the fall of Constantinople in which sages from seventeen nations and religions debate in heaven and discover that there is “one religion in the variety of rites”.

fuentes/la-paz-de-la-fe/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the great texts of interreligious dialogue.

fuentes/diferencias-entre-platon-y-arist.texto: On the Differences between Plato and Aristotle
Short treatise written in Florence during the council that criticizes Aristotle in theology, physics and ethics, and defends the superiority of Plato.
It opened the 15th-century controversy between Platonists and Aristotelians and the reception of Plato in the Renaissance.

fuentes/tratado-de-las-leyes/resumen.texto: Work that proposed a philosophical religion with the Greek gods as metaphysical principles, a liturgy and an organization of society.

fuentes/tratado-de-las-leyes/por_que_imp.texto: Gennadios Scholarios had it burned c. 1460; the fragments he himself quoted and a table of contents survive.

fuentes/contra-el-calumniador-de-platon/.texto: Defense of Plato against George of Trebizond, who accused him of immorality and of being an enemy of Christianity. Bessarion argues that Plato and Aristotle agree on essentials and that Plato is closer to the faith.
It was the first complete presentation of Platonic philosophy printed in Latin.

fuentes/teologia-platonica/resumen.texto: Treatise in eighteen books that defends the immortality of the soul with Platonic arguments and presents the human soul as the center of the universe, the link between the divine and the corporeal.

fuentes/teologia-platonica/por_que_impor.texto: It is the main work of Florentine Platonism; its influence reaches the Lateran Council of 1513, which declared the individual immortality of the soul a dogma.

fuentes/platon-de-ficino/resumen.texto: Latin translation of all of Plato's dialogues with introductions, commissioned by Cosimo de' Medici. It was printed in 1484.

fuentes/platon-de-ficino/por_que_importa.texto: It was the gateway to Plato for all of Europe for three centuries.

fuentes/oracion-sobre-la-dignidad-del-ho.texto: Oration on the Dignity of Man

Speech written to open the debate on the 900 theses: God made the human being without a fixed nature so that he might shape himself, and all traditions of wisdom, from the Chaldeans to the Kabbalah, agree on the truth.
It is the most quoted text of Renaissance humanism; the title was given to it later.

fuentes/donacion-de-constantino-falsa/ti.texto: On the Forged Donation of Constantine

fuentes/donacion-de-constantino-falsa/re.texto: Speech demonstrating that the document by which Constantine supposedly ceded dominion over the West to the pope is a forgery: its Latin, its titles and its anachronisms cannot date from the 4th century.

fuentes/donacion-de-constantino-falsa/po.texto: It is a landmark of historical and philological criticism; Valla wrote it in the service of Alfonso V, an enemy of the pope.

fuentes/donacion-de-constantino-falsa/le.texto: Latin edition with English translation by C. B. Coleman (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/dialogo-de-catalina/resumen.texto: Mystical dialogue between the soul and God on truth, discretion, prayer and providence, with the image of Christ as a bridge between heaven and earth.

fuentes/dialogo-de-catalina/por_que_impo.texto: It is a classic of Italian prose and of mysticism.

fuentes/revelaciones-del-amor-divino/res.texto: Account of and meditation on sixteen visions that Julian had in 1373, during a serious illness, in a short version and a long one written twenty years later. It speaks of God as mother and affirms that “all shall be well”.

fuentes/revelaciones-del-amor-divino/por.texto: It is the first book in English known to have been written by a woman.

fuentes/revelaciones-del-amor-divino/lee.texto: Modern English edition by Grace Warrack (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/la-ciudad-de-las-damas/titulo.texto: The Book of the City of Ladies

fuentes/la-ciudad-de-las-damas/resumen.texto: Allegory in which Reason, Rectitude and Justice help Christine build a city for the illustrious women of history, in response to the authors who denigrated them.

fuentes/la-ciudad-de-las-damas/por_que_i.texto: It is a reasoned defense of the intellectual and moral dignity of women; it opens the so-called “querelle des femmes”.

fuentes/divina-comedia/resumen.texto: Poem in three parts and one hundred cantos in which Dante, guided by Virgil and then by Beatrice, travels through Hell, Purgatory and Paradise during Holy Week of 1300, and meets figures from history and from his own time.

fuentes/divina-comedia/por_que_importa.texto: It sums up medieval cosmology, philosophy and theology, from Aristotle to Thomas Aquinas, and is the founding work of Italian literature.

fuentes/divina-comedia/leer.2.titulo.texto: English translation by H. W. Longfellow (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/monarquia/resumen.texto: Treatise in three books arguing that humanity needs a universal monarch for peace, that this power belonged to the Romans and that it comes directly from God, not from the pope.

fuentes/monarquia/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great medieval defense of the autonomy of temporal power; it was on the Index of Forbidden Books until 1881.

fuentes/monarquia/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by F. J. Church, with an essay by R. W. Church (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/biblioteca-de-focio/resumen.texto: Summaries and critical assessments of 279 books that Photius read, by historians, orators, physicians, novelists, theologians and Church Fathers.

fuentes/biblioteca-de-focio/por_que_impo.texto: It is the only source for many lost ancient works, such as parts of Ctesias, Diodorus or Memnon.

fuentes/cronografia/resumen.texto: History of the Byzantine emperors from Basil II to Michael VII, with psychological portraits and recollections of what the author saw at court.

fuentes/cronografia/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the masterpieces of Byzantine historiography.

fuentes/triadas/titulo.texto: Triads in Defense of the Holy Hesychasts

fuentes/triadas/resumen.texto: Three sets of three treatises against Barlaam of Calabria that defend hesychast prayer and distinguish in God between the unknowable essence and the uncreated energies, which the saints can see as light.

fuentes/triadas/por_que_importa.texto: It founded Palamite theology, accepted by the Orthodox Church in the councils of 1341 to 1351.

fuentes/liber-abaci/soporte.texto: Manuscripts of the revised version of 1228

fuentes/liber-abaci/resumen.texto: Book of calculation in fifteen chapters that teaches how to write numbers with the nine Indian figures and zero, and how to solve problems of trade, currency exchange, partnerships, roots and equations. It includes the rabbit problem that gives the Fibonacci sequence.

fuentes/liber-abaci/por_que_importa.texto: It spread the numeral system we use today among the merchants of Europe.

fuentes/tratado-de-la-esfera/soporte.texto: Manuscripts; more than two hundred printed editions

fuentes/tratado-de-la-esfera/resumen.texto: Astronomy textbook in four chapters: the spherical shape of the world and of the Earth, the circles of the celestial sphere, the rising and setting of the stars, and the motions of the planets and eclipses.

fuentes/tratado-de-la-esfera/por_que_imp.texto: It was the basic astronomy text in all universities until the 17th century.

fuentes/carta-sobre-el-iman/resumen.texto: Letter to a friend, dated 8 August 1269 in the camp of the siege of Lucera, that describes the poles of a spherical magnet, how to find them, how they attract and repel each other, and two compasses.

fuentes/carta-sobre-el-iman/por_que_impo.texto: It is the first known experimental treatise on magnetism; William Gilbert cited it in 1600.

fuentes/tablas-toledanas/resumen.texto: Astronomical tables prepared in Toledo by a group of astronomers led by Arzachel to calculate the positions of the Sun, the Moon and the planets, and eclipses.

fuentes/tablas-toledanas/por_que_importa.texto: Translated into Latin in the 12th century, they were used throughout Europe until they were replaced by the Alfonsine Tables.

fuentes/tablas-alfonsies/resumen.texto: Astronomical tables prepared in Toledo by the Jewish astronomers Isaac ibn Sid and Judah ben Moses for Alfonso X, calculated for the meridian of Toledo.

fuentes/tablas-alfonsies/por_que_importa.texto: They were Europe's standard astronomical tables until the 16th century; Copernicus used them.

fuentes/kitab-al-tasrif/resumen.texto: Medical encyclopedia in thirty books. The last one, on surgery, describes operations, cauterizations, childbirth and fractures, with drawings of the instruments.

fuentes/kitab-al-tasrif/por_que_importa.texto: Translated into Latin by Gerard of Cremona, it was the surgical textbook of European universities for five centuries.

fuentes/pantegni/resumen.texto: Latin adaptation of the Royal Book by Ali ibn al-Abbas al-Majusi, a 10th-century Persian physician: an encyclopedia of medical theory and practice.

fuentes/pantegni/por_que_importa.texto: It was the first major text of Arabic medicine in Latin and the basis of teaching at Salerno.

fuentes/trotula/autor.texto: Trota of Salerno and other Salernitan authors

fuentes/trotula/resumen.texto: Set of three treatises from Salerno on women's medicine: on the diseases of women, on their treatments and on cosmetics. The second is attributed to Trota.

fuentes/trotula/por_que_importa.texto: It was the most widely circulated work on gynecology in Europe until the 15th century.

fuentes/micrologus/resumen.texto: Treatise on practical music that explains scales, intervals, how to compose a melody and the earliest forms of polyphony (organum).

fuentes/micrologus/por_que_importa.texto: After Boethius, it was the most copied music treatise of the Middle Ages.

fuentes/espejo-mayor/resumen.texto: Encyclopedia in three parts, the mirror of nature, the mirror of doctrine and the mirror of history, with excerpts from hundreds of ancient and medieval authors arranged by subject.

fuentes/espejo-mayor/por_que_importa.texto: It was the largest encyclopedia of the Middle Ages, with some 4.5 million words.

fuentes/leyenda-dorada/soporte.texto: More than a thousand manuscripts; one of the first printed books in many languages

fuentes/leyenda-dorada/resumen.texto: Collection of saints' lives and explanations of feasts arranged according to the liturgical year.

fuentes/leyenda-dorada/por_que_importa.texto: It was the most widely read book in Europe after the Bible at the end of the Middle Ages and the source of the iconography of the saints.

fuentes/leyenda-dorada/leer.1.titulo.texto: French translation by Teodor de Wyzewa (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/historia-de-los-francos/resumen.texto: History in ten books from the creation of the world to 591, centered on Gaul under the Merovingian kings, their civil wars, their bishops and their miracles. The last books recount what Gregory witnessed as bishop of Tours.

fuentes/historia-de-los-francos/por_que_.texto: It is the main source for the Gaul of the 5th and 6th centuries, including the baptism of Clovis. It also records the name that a temple in Clermont, destroyed by the Alemanni, had “in the Gaulish language”: Vasso Galatae (I.32), one of the late witnesses to the Gaulish language.

fuentes/historia-de-los-francos/leer.1.t.texto: English translation by Ernest Brehaut, selection (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/getica/titulo.texto: Getica (The Origin and Deeds of the Goths)

fuentes/getica/resumen.texto: History of the Goths from their supposed origin in Scandinavia to the defeat of the Ostrogoths by Justinian, summarized from the lost history of Cassiodorus. It includes the Battle of the Catalaunian Plains against Attila. It also tells (XLV.237-238) that Riothamus, king of the Britons, came with twelve thousand men to help the Romans against the Visigoth Euric and was defeated around 469.

fuentes/getica/por_que_importa.texto: It is almost the only source on the origin of the Goths and on Attila's Huns.

fuentes/getica/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by C. C. Mierow (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/historia-de-las-guerras/resumen.texto: Eight books on Justinian's wars against the Persians, the Vandals of North Africa and the Ostrogoths of Italy, which Procopius witnessed as Belisarius's secretary. It describes the plague of 541.

fuentes/historia-de-las-guerras/por_que_.texto: It is the main source for the 6th-century Mediterranean and for the Byzantine reconquest of Italy.

fuentes/historia-de-las-guerras/leer.0.t.texto: English translation by H. B. Dewing: the Persian War (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/historia-de-las-guerras/leer.1.t.texto: English translation: the Vandalic War (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/historia-de-las-guerras/leer.2.t.texto: English translation: the Gothic War, books V and VI (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/historia-secreta/soporte.texto: Manuscripts; discovered in the Vatican Library in 1623

fuentes/historia-secreta/resumen.texto: Unpublished lampoon against Justinian, Theodora, Belisarius and his wife Antonina, which contradicts the tone of Procopius's public works.

fuentes/historia-secreta/por_que_importa.texto: It shows the other side of Justinian's court, although its exaggeration requires it to be read with care.

fuentes/corpus-iuris-civilis/soporte.texto: Manuscripts; the Digest, in the 6th-century Florentine codex

fuentes/corpus-iuris-civilis/resumen.texto: Compilation of Roman law ordered by Justinian and directed by Tribonian: the Code of imperial laws, the Digest of jurists' opinions, the Institutes for students and the Novels, later laws.

fuentes/corpus-iuris-civilis/por_que_imp.texto: Rediscovered in Bologna c. 1070, it became the basis of European civil law and of the University of Bologna.

fuentes/variae/resumen.texto: Collection of 468 letters and official documents that Cassiodorus drafted for the Ostrogothic kings: appointments, orders, diplomacy and administration.

fuentes/variae/por_que_importa.texto: It shows how Roman government worked under the Gothic kings.

fuentes/historia-de-los-lombardos/resume.texto: History of the Lombards in six books from their legendary origin in Scandinavia to the death of King Liutprand in 744. It was left unfinished.

fuentes/historia-de-los-lombardos/por_qu.texto: It is the main source for the Lombard kingdom of Italy.

fuentes/vida-de-carlomagno/resumen.texto: Biography of Charlemagne by a man of his court, following the model of Suetonius's Lives of the Caesars: wars, government, family, physical appearance, habits and death.

fuentes/vida-de-carlomagno/por_que_impor.texto: It is the main source on Charlemagne as a person and the first biography of a layman in the Middle Ages.

fuentes/vida-de-carlomagno/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by A. J. Grant (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/manual-de-dhuoda/resumen.texto: Book of moral, religious and political advice that Dhuoda wrote for her son William, a hostage at the court of Charles the Bald: how to serve God, his father and his lord.

fuentes/manual-de-dhuoda/por_que_importa.texto: It is one of the few works by a laywoman from the Carolingian period and a source on the education of the nobility.

fuentes/cronica-anglosajona/resumen.texto: Annals in Old English begun at the court of Alfred the Great and continued in several monasteries: Viking invasions, kings, bishops, comets and famines, year by year.

fuentes/cronica-anglosajona/por_que_impo.texto: It is the oldest chronicle written in a European language other than Latin and Greek that was continued for centuries.

fuentes/cronica-anglosajona/leer.1.titul.texto: English translation by James Ingram (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/beowulf/soporte.texto: A single manuscript, Cotton Vitellius A.xv (c. 1000)

fuentes/beowulf/resumen.texto: Heroic poem of 3182 lines about Beowulf, a Geatish warrior who kills the monster Grendel and his mother at the court of the Danish king Hrothgar, and who in old age dies killing a dragon.

fuentes/beowulf/por_que_importa.texto: It is the longest poem in Old English and a source on the values of the Germanic aristocracy; the manuscript was nearly lost in the fire of 1731.

fuentes/beowulf/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by F. B. Gummere (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/libro-de-kells/resumen.texto: Manuscript of the four Gospels with extraordinarily complex decorations: interlace, animals and full-page figures. It is debated whether it was begun on Iona before the Viking attacks of 806 and finished at Kells; the Annals of Ulster record that in 1007 they stole from Kells “the great gospel book of Columba”, which is usually identified with it. It has been at Trinity College Dublin since the 17th century.

fuentes/libro-de-kells/por_que_importa.texto: It is the masterpiece of Insular illumination from Ireland and Britain.

fuentes/relacion-de-la-embajada/titulo.texto: Report on the Embassy to Constantinople

fuentes/relacion-de-la-embajada/resumen.texto: Report to Otto I on the failed embassy of 968 to Emperor Nikephoros Phokas to request a Byzantine princess for the future Otto II: banquets, snubs and arguments over the imperial title.

fuentes/relacion-de-la-embajada/por_que_.texto: It is one of the liveliest descriptions of the Byzantine court as seen by a Westerner.

fuentes/hechos-de-los-obispos-de-hamburg.texto: Deeds of the Bishops of the Hamburg Church

History of the archbishopric of Hamburg-Bremen and of the mission in the north, with a fourth book describing the islands and peoples of the Baltic and the North Atlantic, the pagan temple at Uppsala, Iceland, Greenland and Vinland.
It contains the first written mention of Vinland and is a main source for Viking Age Scandinavia.

fuentes/cronica-de-nestor/idioma_origina.texto: Old Church Slavonic with East Slavic features

fuentes/cronica-de-nestor/resumen.texto: History of the Rus from the division of the world among the sons of Noah: the calling of the Varangians, the first princes of Kiev, the baptism of Vladimir in 988 and the struggles among the princes up to 1110.

fuentes/cronica-de-nestor/por_que_import.texto: It is the main source for Kievan Rus, although it mixes legend and history.

fuentes/justicia-rusa/autor.texto: Yaroslav the Wise and his successors

fuentes/justicia-rusa/soporte.texto: Copies from the 13th to the 15th century

fuentes/justicia-rusa/resumen.texto: Law code of Kievan Rus in a short version, attributed to Yaroslav and his sons, and an expanded 12th-century version: blood feud, fines for homicide and injury, debts, inheritance and serfs.

fuentes/justicia-rusa/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first law code of the East Slavs.

fuentes/cronica-de-los-bohemios/resumen.texto: History of Bohemia in three books from the mythical arrival of Father Čech and Princess Libuše to the author's own time.

fuentes/cronica-de-los-bohemios/por_que_.texto: It is the main source for the early Přemyslids.

fuentes/hechos-de-los-daneses/soporte.texto: Manuscript fragments; printed edition of Paris (1514)

fuentes/hechos-de-los-daneses/resumen.texto: History of Denmark in sixteen books from the legendary kings, with many sagas and legends, to the wars of Valdemar I and Absalon against the Wends.

fuentes/hechos-de-los-daneses/por_que_im.texto: It preserves lost Scandinavian heroic traditions, such as that of Amleth, which Shakespeare transformed into Hamlet.

fuentes/hechos-de-los-daneses/leer.1.tit.texto: English translation by Oliver Elton, books I-IX (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/libro-de-los-islandeses/resumen.texto: Short history of Iceland: the settlement from 870, the founding of the Althing in 930, the discovery of Greenland, the conversion to Christianity in the year 1000 and the first bishops.

fuentes/libro-de-los-islandeses/por_que_.texto: It is the first historical work in Old Norse and the basis of Icelandic chronology.

fuentes/edda-poetica/resumen.texto: Collection of mythological and heroic poems: the Völuspá on the origin and end of the world, Odin's counsels in the Hávamál and the lays of Sigurd and the Nibelungs.

fuentes/edda-poetica/por_que_importa.texto: It is the main source for Norse mythology; the poems predate the manuscript, although their date is debated.

fuentes/edda-poetica/leer.0.titulo.texto: Völuspá in Old Norse on Wikisource

fuentes/edda-poetica/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by Henry Adams Bellows (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/edda-prosaica/resumen.texto: Handbook for poets in four parts: a prologue, the Gylfaginning with the myths of the Norse gods, the Skáldskaparmál on poetic language and the Háttatal, a poem illustrating the metres.

fuentes/edda-prosaica/por_que_importa.texto: Together with the Poetic Edda, it is the main source for Norse mythology.

fuentes/edda-prosaica/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation by R. B. Anderson (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/heimskringla/resumen.texto: Sagas of the kings of Norway from the legendary Ynglings to 1177, including the conversion of Norway and the death of Harald Hardrada at Stamford Bridge.

fuentes/heimskringla/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great historical work of medieval Scandinavia.

fuentes/heimskringla/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by Samuel Laing (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/saga-de-njal/resumen.texto: The longest of the sagas of Icelanders: a feud between families that ends with the burning of the house of the wise lawyer Njál, with scenes at the Althing and of the conversion.

fuentes/saga-de-njal/por_que_importa.texto: It is the masterpiece of Icelandic prose and a source on the law and society of medieval Iceland.

fuentes/saga-de-njal/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by G. W. Dasent (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/historia-de-los-reyes-de-britani.texto: History of the Kings of Britain

Legendary history of the Britons from their Trojan founder Brutus to the 7th century, with the kings Lear and Cymbeline, the magician Merlin and the reign of Arthur. Geoffrey says he translated it from “a very ancient book in the British language” given to him by Walter, archdeacon of Oxford, which no one has found; he used Gildas, Bede and the Historia Brittonum.

It spread the Arthurian legend across Europe. William of Newburgh already called it an invention around 1198, and historians today debate whether there was a real figure behind Arthur: Alcock (1971) defended it; Dumville, Padel and Halsall doubt it.

fuentes/domesday-book/soporte.texto: Two parchment volumes (The National Archives, Kew)

fuentes/domesday-book/resumen.texto: Record of the lands, lords, peasants, mills and livestock of almost all of England, ordered by William the Conqueror in 1085 to find out what he held and what was owed to him.

fuentes/domesday-book/por_que_importa.texto: It is the most complete survey of medieval Europe and the basis for estimating the English population in 1086.

fuentes/tapiz-de-bayeux/soporte.texto: Wool embroidery on linen, almost 70 metres long

fuentes/tapiz-de-bayeux/resumen.texto: Embroidery that tells in scenes the story of the Norman Conquest: Harold's journey to Normandy, his oath, his coronation, William's fleet and the Battle of Hastings.

fuentes/tapiz-de-bayeux/por_que_importa.texto: It is a unique visual source on 11th-century weapons, ships, clothing and customs.

fuentes/carta-magna/autor.texto: King John and the barons of England

fuentes/carta-magna/resumen.texto: Agreement sealed on 15 June 1215 between King John and the rebel barons: it guarantees the rights of the Church, limits feudal levies and promises that no free man shall be imprisoned without the lawful judgement of his peers.

fuentes/carta-magna/por_que_importa.texto: It became the symbol of government subject to law and of liberties against power.

fuentes/cronica-mayor/resumen.texto: Universal chronicle that becomes detailed for 1235-1259, with news from all over Europe, of the Mongols and of the East, copied documents and drawings by the author himself, such as King Henry III's elephant.

fuentes/cronica-mayor/por_que_importa.texto: It is the principal European chronicle of the mid-13th century.

fuentes/cantar-de-roldan/autor.texto: Anonymous (Turold, according to the last line)

fuentes/cantar-de-roldan/resumen.texto: Chanson de geste about the death of Roland, Charlemagne's nephew, in the rearguard of the Frankish army attacked at Roncevaux through Ganelon's treachery, and the emperor's revenge.

fuentes/cantar-de-roldan/por_que_importa.texto: It is the great French epic and turns a Basque ambush of 778 into a war against Islam.

fuentes/cantar-de-roldan/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation by C. K. Scott-Moncrieff (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/cantar-de-mio-cid/soporte.texto: A single manuscript, a 14th-century copy of Per Abbat's text (1207) (National Library of Spain)

fuentes/cantar-de-mio-cid/resumen.texto: Chanson de geste about the exile of Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, his campaigns, the conquest of Valencia and the outrage committed against his daughters by the Infantes of Carrión.

fuentes/cantar-de-mio-cid/por_que_import.texto: It is the first great surviving poem of Spanish literature; the date and place of composition are debated.

fuentes/cantar-de-mio-cid/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text in medieval Castilian on Wikisource

fuentes/cantar-de-mio-cid/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by R. S. Rose and L. Bacon (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/cantar-de-los-nibelungos/soporte.texto: Three main manuscripts (A, B and C)

fuentes/cantar-de-los-nibelungos/resumen.texto: Epic about Siegfried, slayer of a dragon, his murder at the court of the Burgundians in Worms and the revenge of his widow Kriemhild at the court of Attila.

fuentes/cantar-de-los-nibelungos/por_que.texto: It preserves the memory of the destruction of the Burgundian kingdom by the Huns in 437.

fuentes/cantar-de-los-nibelungos/leer.0..texto: English translation by D. B. Shumway (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/parzival/soporte.texto: More than eighty manuscripts and fragments

fuentes/parzival/resumen.texto: Verse romance about a naive young man who arrives at Arthur's court, fails on his first visit to the Grail castle and, after years of searching, becomes its king.

fuentes/parzival/por_que_importa.texto: It is the most complete version of the Grail legend and a high point of German literature; Wagner adapted it as an opera.

fuentes/parzival/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation by Jessie L. Weston, volume 1 (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/parzival/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by Jessie L. Weston, volume 2 (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/lancelot/titulo.texto: Lancelot, the Knight of the Cart

fuentes/lancelot/resumen.texto: Verse romance in which Lancelot rescues Queen Guinevere and climbs into the cart of the condemned for love of her, written for Marie de Champagne.

fuentes/lancelot/por_que_importa.texto: It is the first great work of courtly love applied to the Arthurian matter.

fuentes/lancelot/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation by W. W. Comfort, in Four Arthurian Romances (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/canciones-de-guillermo-ix/resume.texto: Eleven songs by the Duke of Aquitaine, some burlesque and obscene, others of courtly love, and one of farewell before departing.

fuentes/canciones-de-guillermo-ix/por_qu.texto: They are the oldest troubadour poems and the beginning of lyric poetry in a Romance language.

fuentes/roman-de-la-rose/autor.texto: Guillaume de Lorris and Jean de Meun

fuentes/roman-de-la-rose/resumen.texto: Allegorical poem about the winning of a rose in a garden, begun by Guillaume de Lorris c. 1230 and continued by Jean de Meun c. 1275, who turned it into a satirical encyclopedia on nature, love and society.

fuentes/roman-de-la-rose/por_que_importa.texto: It was the most widely read book in French in the Middle Ages, and its misogyny provoked the response of Christine de Pizan.

fuentes/roman-de-la-rose/leer.0.titulo.texto: Text in Old French, volume I (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/carmina-burana/idioma_original.texto: Latin, with lines in German and French

fuentes/carmina-burana/soporte.texto: A manuscript found at Benediktbeuern in 1803

fuentes/carmina-burana/resumen.texto: About 250 poems and songs by wandering clerics: satires against the Church, songs of love, drinking and gambling, and religious dramas.

fuentes/carmina-burana/por_que_importa.texto: It is the largest collection of goliardic poetry; Carl Orff set several of the poems to music in 1937.

fuentes/cantigas-de-santa-maria/soporte.texto: Four codices with music and miniatures (El Escorial, Toledo and Florence)

fuentes/cantigas-de-santa-maria/resumen.texto: Collection of 420 songs to the Virgin with their music, most of them accounts of miracles, composed in the workshop of Alfonso X; the codices contain miniatures of daily life.

fuentes/cantigas-de-santa-maria/por_que_.texto: It is one of the largest collections of medieval music and a visual source for 13th-century Castile.

fuentes/siete-partidas/resumen.texto: Code in seven parts on the Church, the king, justice, marriage, contracts, inheritance and criminal law, inspired by Roman and canon law.

fuentes/siete-partidas/por_que_importa.texto: It was in force in Castile and the Americas for centuries and was a source for the 19th-century codes.

fuentes/estoria-de-espanna/resumen.texto: History of Spain from the first settlers to Ferdinand III, compiled in the workshop of Alfonso X from Latin and Arabic chronicles and chansons de geste.

fuentes/estoria-de-espanna/por_que_impor.texto: It is the first general history of Spain written in Castilian.

fuentes/conde-lucanor/resumen.texto: Fifty-one tales in which the counsellor Patronio answers his lord's questions with an example and a moral in verse; several come from Arabic and Eastern sources.

fuentes/conde-lucanor/por_que_importa.texto: It is a masterpiece of Castilian prose and one of the first story collections in Europe.

fuentes/libro-de-buen-amor/resumen.texto: Verse account of the archpriest's amorous adventures, with fables, prayers, satires and the battle between Don Carnal and Doña Cuaresma.

fuentes/libro-de-buen-amor/por_que_impor.texto: It is one of the great works of medieval Spanish poetry, with a deliberate ambiguity between the love of God and worldly love.

fuentes/decameron/resumen.texto: One hundred stories told over ten days by ten young people who take refuge in the countryside from the Florentine plague of 1348. The introduction describes the epidemic.

fuentes/decameron/por_que_importa.texto: It is the founding work of Italian prose and a source on the Black Death.

fuentes/decameron/leer.1.titulo.texto: English translation by John Payne (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/cancionero-de-petrarca/escrita.l.texto: Avignon, Vaucluse, Milan, Padua and Arquà

fuentes/cancionero-de-petrarca/soporte.texto: Manuscript in the hand of the author and his copyist (Vatican, Lat. 3195)

fuentes/cancionero-de-petrarca/resumen.texto: Collection of 366 poems, mostly sonnets, dedicated to Laura, whom Petrarch says he saw in Avignon in 1327, before and after her death in the plague of 1348.

fuentes/cancionero-de-petrarca/por_que_i.texto: It was the model for European lyric poetry for three centuries.

fuentes/cancionero-de-petrarca/leer.1.ti.texto: English translation by various authors (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/cuentos-de-canterbury/soporte.texto: More than eighty manuscripts; printed by Caxton in 1476

fuentes/cuentos-de-canterbury/resumen.texto: Twenty-four tales in verse and prose told by pilgrims of every rank, from the knight to the miller, on the way to the shrine of Thomas Becket at Canterbury.

fuentes/cuentos-de-canterbury/por_que_im.texto: It is the founding work of literature in English and a portrait of 14th-century English society.

fuentes/cuentos-de-canterbury/leer.0.tit.texto: Text in Middle English, edited by W. W. Skeat (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/libro-de-las-maravillas/titulo.texto: Book of the Marvels of the World

fuentes/libro-de-las-maravillas/resumen.texto: Account of Marco Polo's travels through Asia and his stay at the court of Kublai Khan, dictated in prison in Genoa to Rustichello da Pisa: cities, products, customs, paper money and reports of Japan.

fuentes/libro-de-las-maravillas/por_que_.texto: It was the main European source on Asia until the 16th century; Columbus carried an annotated copy.

fuentes/libro-de-las-maravillas/leer.0.t.texto: English translation by Henry Yule, volume 1 (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/libro-de-las-maravillas/leer.1.t.texto: English translation by Henry Yule, volume 2 (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/nueva-cronica/resumen.texto: History of Florence from the Tower of Babel to 1348, detailed for the 13th and 14th centuries, with exceptional data on population, schools, banks, churches and prices.

fuentes/nueva-cronica/por_que_importa.texto: It is a main source for the economy and society of a great medieval city; Villani died in the plague before finishing it.

fuentes/nueva-cronica/leer.1.titulo.texto: English selection by Rose Selfe and P. H. Wicksteed (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/cronicas-de-froissart/soporte.texto: More than a hundred manuscripts, many of them illuminated

fuentes/cronicas-de-froissart/resumen.texto: History of the Hundred Years' War and of the courts of France, England, Scotland and the Iberian Peninsula, told from eyewitness accounts: Crécy, Poitiers, the Jacquerie, the revolt of 1381.

fuentes/cronicas-de-froissart/por_que_im.texto: It is the most famous source on 14th-century chivalry, although of variable accuracy.

fuentes/cronicas-de-froissart/leer.0.tit.texto: French edition by Siméon Luce, volume 1 (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/conquista-de-constantinopla/resu.texto: Account of the Fourth Crusade by one of its leaders: the preaching, the agreement with Venice, the diversion to Zara and Constantinople, the sack of 1204 and the first years of the Latin Empire.

fuentes/conquista-de-constantinopla/por_.texto: It is one of the first works of history in French prose and the crusaders' version of 1204.

fuentes/conquista-de-constantinopla/leer.texto: English translation by Frank Marzials (Project Gutenberg)

fuentes/vida-de-san-luis/resumen.texto: Memoirs of the seneschal of Champagne about Louis IX, written for Queen Joan of Navarre, with the account of the Seventh Crusade in Egypt, on which Joinville accompanied the king.

fuentes/vida-de-san-luis/por_que_importa.texto: It is an exceptionally vivid and personal portrait of a medieval king.

fuentes/espejo-de-sajonia/idioma_origina.texto: Middle Low German (and a lost Latin version)

fuentes/espejo-de-sajonia/soporte.texto: More than 400 manuscripts, four of them illustrated

fuentes/espejo-de-sajonia/resumen.texto: Compilation of the customary law of Saxony: territorial law (inheritance, crimes, courts) and feudal law.

fuentes/espejo-de-sajonia/por_que_import.texto: It is the most important law book of medieval Germany and one of the first works of German prose; it was applied in parts of Germany until 1900.

fuentes/bula-de-oro/soporte.texto: Seven original copies with a gold seal

fuentes/bula-de-oro/resumen.texto: Law of the Holy Roman Empire that establishes the election of the King of the Romans by a majority of seven prince-electors (the Archbishops of Mainz, Cologne and Trier, the King of Bohemia, the Count Palatine, the Duke of Saxony and the Margrave of Brandenburg).

fuentes/bula-de-oro/por_que_importa.texto: It was the constitution of the Empire until its dissolution in 1806.

fuentes/decreto-de-graciano/resumen.texto: Compilation of about 3800 texts of Church law (conciliar canons, papal decrees, texts of the Fathers) arranged to resolve their contradictions.

fuentes/decreto-de-graciano/por_que_impo.texto: It founded the science of canon law and was the first part of the Corpus iuris canonici, in force until 1917.

fuentes/dictatus-papae/soporte.texto: Register of Gregory VII's letters (Vatican Archives)

fuentes/dictatus-papae/resumen.texto: List of 27 statements on the power of the pope: he alone can depose bishops and emperors, no one may judge him and the Roman Church has never erred.

fuentes/dictatus-papae/por_que_importa.texto: It sums up the program of the Gregorian reform that led to the Investiture Controversy.

fuentes/concordato-de-worms-texto/autor.texto: Henry V and Pope Calixtus II

fuentes/concordato-de-worms-texto/resume.texto: Agreement of 23 September 1122 by which the emperor renounces investing bishops with the ring and crosier, and the pope accepts that the emperor grant them their temporal possessions with the sceptre.

fuentes/concordato-de-worms-texto/por_qu.texto: It ended the Investiture Controversy and distinguished the spiritual from the temporal power of bishops.

fuentes/unam-sanctam/resumen.texto: Bull of 18 November 1302, issued at the height of the dispute with Philip IV, which asserts that there are two swords, the spiritual and the temporal, both in the power of the Church, and that submission to the Roman pontiff is necessary for salvation.

fuentes/unam-sanctam/por_que_importa.texto: It is the most extreme assertion of papal supremacy in the Middle Ages.

fuentes/liber-iudiciorum/soporte.texto: Manuscripts; translated into Castilian as the Fuero Juzgo in 1241

fuentes/liber-iudiciorum/resumen.texto: Visigothic law code in twelve books, promulgated by Recceswinth in 654 for Goths and Hispano-Romans alike.

fuentes/liber-iudiciorum/por_que_importa.texto: It was the common law of the Christian kingdoms of the Iberian Peninsula for centuries.

fuentes/cronica-de-alfonso-iii/autor.texto: Court of Alfonso III of Asturias

fuentes/cronica-de-alfonso-iii/resumen.texto: Chronicle of the Visigothic and Asturian kings from Wamba to Ordoño I, with the account of Covadonga and the idea that the kings of Asturias are heirs of the Goths.

fuentes/cronica-de-alfonso-iii/por_que_i.texto: It is a primary source for the origins of the Kingdom of Asturias and for the ideology of the Reconquista.

fuentes/cronica-mozarabe/resumen.texto: Chronicle by a Christian who lived under Muslim rule: the last Visigothic kings, the Arab conquest of 711 and the first governors of al-Andalus, including the Battle of Poitiers.

fuentes/cronica-mozarabe/por_que_importa.texto: It is the closest source to the conquest of 711 and mentions the “europenses” at Poitiers.

fuentes/hechos-de-los-francos/resumen.texto: Account of the First Crusade by a participant in the army of Bohemond of Taranto: the Council of Clermont, the siege of Antioch and the conquest of Jerusalem.

fuentes/hechos-de-los-francos/por_que_im.texto: It is the most direct testimony of the First Crusade and was the basis for several later chronicles.

fuentes/alexiada/resumen.texto: History of the reign of Alexios I Komnenos in fifteen books: the wars against the Normans, the Pechenegs and the Turks, and the passage of the First Crusade through Constantinople as seen from Byzantium.

fuentes/alexiada/por_que_importa.texto: It is the main Byzantine view of the Crusades and the earliest surviving work of history written by a woman.

fuentes/alexiada/leer.0.titulo.texto: English translation by Elizabeth Dawes on Wikisource

fuentes/viaje-de-ibn-yubair/resumen.texto: Diary of the journey to Mecca between 1183 and 1185: Egypt in the time of Saladin, Arabia, Syria, the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem and Norman Sicily, where Muslims lived under a Christian king.

fuentes/viaje-de-ibn-yubair/por_que_impo.texto: It is an exceptional source on coexistence and trade between Christians and Muslims in the 12th-century Mediterranean.

fuentes/libro-de-roger/resumen.texto: Geography of the known world commissioned by Roger II: it divides the world into seven climes and seventy sections, with a map for each, and descriptions of cities, routes and distances gathered from travelers and books.

fuentes/libro-de-roger/por_que_importa.texto: It was the most complete geography of its time, for both Europe and the Islamic world.

fuentes/biblia-de-gutenberg/soporte.texto: About 180 copies printed on paper and parchment; 49 survive

fuentes/biblia-de-gutenberg/resumen.texto: Latin Bible printed with movable metal type in two columns of 42 lines, in Gutenberg's workshop with Johann Fust and Peter Schöffer.

fuentes/biblia-de-gutenberg/por_que_impo.texto: It was the first major printed book in Europe: it opened the age of printing.

fuentes/martillo-de-las-brujas/soporte.texto: Printed in Speyer in 1486, with some thirty editions up to 1669

fuentes/martillo-de-las-brujas/resumen.texto: Treatise by a Dominican inquisitor that defines witchcraft as heresy, attributes it mainly to women and gives instructions for prosecuting it.

fuentes/martillo-de-las-brujas/por_que_i.texto: It contributed to the witch hunts of the 16th and 17th centuries, although the Inquisition advised against it.

fuentes/anales-de-polonia/titulo.texto: Annals of the Famous Kingdom of Poland

fuentes/anales-de-polonia/resumen.texto: History of Poland in twelve books from its legendary origins to 1480, based on chronicles, documents and testimonies, with detailed accounts of the Mongol invasion of 1241 and the Battle of Grunwald.

fuentes/anales-de-polonia/por_que_import.texto: It is the great medieval history of Poland and the main source for Grunwald.

personas/agustin-de-hipona/resumen.texto: Bishop of Hippo, in North Africa, and the most influential Christian thinker of the Latin West. He combined Platonism with the Christian faith; his ideas on grace, the will, time and history shaped all of medieval philosophy.

personas/boecio/resumen.texto: Roman senator in the service of the Ostrogothic king Theodoric. He translated Aristotle's logic into Latin and commented on it, which became the basis of medieval logic for six centuries, and wrote The Consolation of Philosophy in prison before being executed.

personas/casiodoro/resumen.texto: Minister of the Ostrogothic kings in Ravenna and later founder of the monastery of Vivarium, in Calabria, where he organized the copying of manuscripts. His Institutions set the program of the liberal arts for monks.
